literal: Even if blooming in clusters, unscented flower-like are they, who what they learned, to be understood, in detail do not speak.
translation: Those who cannot clearly explain what they have learned so that others can understand are like a bunch of flowers that have bloomed but have no fragrance.
modern: தாம் கற்றவற்றை மற்றவர்கள் புரிந்து கொள்ளும்படி விரிவாக எடுத்துச் சொல்ல முடியாதவர்கள், கொத்தாக மலர்ந்திருந்தாலும் மணம் தராத மலரைப் போன்றவர்கள் ஆவர்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of eloquence and communication skills. A person may have acquired vast knowledge through study, but if they cannot articulate it clearly so that others can comprehend it, their learning remains useless. The poet beautifully compares such individuals to a cluster of flowers that, despite blooming abundantly, fail to spread any fragrance.
